correctness.rationale: The diagonal Rota--Baxter identity forces all values to be square-zero in every characteristic-two commutative algebra. Under independent natural-basis squares this is exactly the annihilator and every annihilator-valued map is RB. For 2D dependent nonzero squares over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\), the entire operator set is represented by one functional into the 1D square-zero subspace; the defining equation reduces exactly to a union of two one-dimensional functional spaces, equal precisely when the generator of \(E^2\) is square-zero. Pointwise-local interpolation yields \(q\) or \(q^2\) maps as appropriate. The remaining cases and projective-line census are exhaustive. Direct enumeration of every labeled 2D multiplication and endomorphism over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_4\), five \(\mathbb F_8\) representatives and all binary chain endomorphisms in dimensions 3 and 4 agrees with formulas. The all-field conclusions rely on symbolic proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: Recent characteristic-zero local Rota--Baxter research exhibits strict enlargement for nilpotent chains, motivating the characteristic boundary. The independent-square theorem resolves an arbitrary-dimensional and structurally defined characteristic-two family, reversing that behavior. The exact 2D theorem identifies a genuine exceptional multiplication geometry and computes both operator sets and the density of exceptions among all labeled tables. This is a complete natural low-dimensional classification rather than a single numerical curiosity or a renaming of known results; it does not claim a general classification for higher-dimensional dependent-square algebras.
